dedupe_keys.name: pedestrian dynamics data archive forschungszentrum julich trajectories and videos of crowd evacuation and bottleneck experiments

description: This archive holds the measured paths of people walking through corridors, bottlenecks, stairs and exits in controlled crowd experiments, the empirical basis for most evacuation and pedestrian simulation models. It is built by the Civil Safety Research institute (IAS-7) of Forschungszentrum Jülich with project partners, and carries its own DOI. Coverage spans laboratory, field and machine-learning datasets from experiments in Germany and elsewhere, including China, listed from newest to oldest with participant statistics. Most entries provide video recordings and head trajectories extracted with the PeTrack software at 16 to 25 frames per second, and some add motion capture, contact pressure, heart rate or questionnaires; data type descriptions follow FAIR principles and a dashboard searches the archive together with external datasets. Files are available as free downloads under the Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 licence, with source attribution requested. Caveats: participants are mostly students in laboratory settings, formats vary between older and newer experiments, and video files are large. Simulation uses: calibrating and validating fundamental diagrams, flow through exits and evacuation times in agent-based crowd and building evacuation models. Related records: the JuPedSim simulator (model-jupedsim) from the same institute is designed to use these data.
